record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: After the complexity gaps in Table 1 are resolved for Pareto-optimal and stable matchings under uncertain preferences, determine the analogous complexity of computing or reasoning about rank-maximal matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain.

evidence.quote: After Pareto optimal and stable matchings, one might consider to investigate other fairness notions under uncertain preferences, such as popular or rank-maximal matchings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bipartite matching market with a finite set of agents A and a finite set of items (or another set of agents) B, where each agent a ∈ A has a strict preference order over an acceptable subset of B. A matching M is rank-maximal if it has the maximum number of agents matched to their first choice, subject to that the maximum number matched to their second choice, and so on lexicographically over the rank-distribution vector.

Now suppose the preferences are uncertain, given in one of the standard uncertainty models:
(i) Lottery model: for each agent a, a probability distribution over linear orders of that agent's acceptable partners is given.
(ii) Compact indifference model: each agent provides a partial order (e.g., a weak order with ties), and the true preference is any linear extension chosen uniformly at random.
(iii) Joint probability model: a probability distribution over complete preference profiles is given explicitly.

For each uncertainty model, determine the computational complexity of the following decision/search problems:
1. (Possibly rank-maximal) Given a matching M, decide whether there exists a realization of the preferences under which M is rank-maximal.
2. (Necessarily rank-maximal) Given a matching M, decide whether M is rank-maximal under every realization of positive probability.
3. (Probability of rank-maximality) Compute the probability that a given matching M is rank-maximal.
4. (Most likely rank-maximal) Compute a matching maximizing the probability of being rank-maximal.

Classify each problem as polynomial-time solvable, NP-hard, #P-hard, or otherwise, in each of the three uncertainty models.
artifact.status_search_result: A search indicates that rank-maximal matchings have been studied extensively under classical and tied preferences, and uncertain-preference frameworks have been analyzed for stable, Pareto-optimal, popular, and dominant matchings. However, a systematic complexity classification of rank-maximal matchings under the standard uncertain-preference models (lottery, compact indifference, joint probability) does not appear to have been carried out. The problem is highlighted as a future direction and appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Popular and Dominant Matchings with Uncertain, Multilayer and Aggregated Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies popular and dominant matchings under uncertain preference models, but does not resolve the rank-maximal case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends uncertain-preference analysis to popular/dominant matchings, leaving rank-maximal matchings as a natural open direction.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes complexity of stable matchings under lottery, compact indifference, and joint probability models.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the template of complexity questions that have been resolved for stable matchings but not yet for rank-maximal matchings.

status_evidence.title: Online Elicitation of Necessarily Optimal Matchings
status_evidence.snippet: Considers necessarily optimal (including rank-maximal) matchings under partial preferences elicited online.
status_evidence.claim: Related but addresses elicitation rather than the full uncertainty-model complexity classification.
